title: Apple (AAPL) Stake Lifted by Whalerock Point Partners LLC
text:
Posted by ABMN Staff on Apr 2nd, 2018 // No Comments 
Whalerock Point Partners LLC grew its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 7.0% in the fourth quarter, according to its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The firm owned 58,820 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after acquiring an additional 3,866 shares during the period. Apple comprises 3.2% of Whalerock Point Partners LLC’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 2nd biggest position. Whalerock Point Partners LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $9,955,000 as of its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. 
Several other institutional investors also recently added to or reduced their stakes in AAPL. Strategic Advisors LLC boosted its holdings in Apple by 2.0% in the 4th quarter. Strategic Advisors LLC now owns 63,208 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $10,697,000 after buying an additional 1,226 shares during the period. Convergence Investment Partners LLC boosted its holdings in Apple by 1.3% in the 4th quarter. Convergence Investment Partners LLC now owns 48,902 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $8,276,000 after buying an additional 623 shares during the period. 440 Investment Group LLC boosted its holdings in Apple by 28.1% in the 4th quarter. 440 Investment Group LLC now owns 21,345 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $3,612,000 after buying an additional 4,686 shares during the period. First Hawaiian Bank boosted its holdings in Apple by 24.3% in the 4th quarter. First Hawaiian Bank now owns 7,168 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,213,000 after buying an additional 1,401 shares during the period. Finally, Gemmer Asset Management LLC boosted its holdings in Apple by 9.0% in the 4th quarter. Gemmer Asset Management LLC now owns 9,439 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,597,000 after buying an additional 782 shares during the period. 61.35% of the stock is owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. AAPL has been the subject of several analyst reports. UBS set a $190.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Friday, January 5th. Morgan Stanley reaffirmed a “buy” rating and issued a $205.00 price objective (up from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a report on Tuesday, January 23rd. Sanford C. Bernstein downgraded shares of Apple from an “outperform” rating to a “market perform” rating and cut their price objective for the stock from $195.00 to $170.00 in a report on Friday, February 2nd. HSBC set a $204.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Tuesday, January 30th. Finally, Vetr upgraded shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $184.49 target price on the stock in a research note on Monday, March 5th. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have assigned a buy rating and one has given a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The company presently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $202.52. Shares of AAPL opened at $167.78 on Monday. The stock has a market cap of $851,317.94, a PE ratio of 17.24, a P/E/G ratio of 1.27 and a beta of 1.25. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74, a quick ratio of 1.20 and a current ratio of 1.24. Apple has a 1-year low of $140.06 and a 1-year high of $183.50. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its earnings results on Thursday, February 1st. The iPhone maker reported $3.89 earnings per share for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $3.82 by $0.07. The firm had revenue of $88.29 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $87.62 billion. Apple had a net margin of 21.13% and a return on equity of 37.37%. The company’s revenue for the quarter was up 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter in the previous year, the firm posted $3.36 EPS. research analysts expect that Apple will post 11.37 EPS for the current year. 
In other news, insider Daniel J. Riccio sold 15,641 shares of Apple stock in a transaction dated Friday, January 5th. The shares were sold at an average price of $174.78, for a total transaction of $2,733,733.98. Following the sale, the insider now owns 13,739 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $2,401,302.42. The sale was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available at the SEC website . Insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock.
